name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB (IQ2_XXS QAT GGUF)

params.value: 74B total / 9B active (card). HF GGUF metadata total 74,042,720,848. Compressed from Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B with Star Elastic; top-k 9 experts per token (parent 22). Arithmetic from the GGUF header: routed experts 15.88 GiB of the 20.50 GiB tensors; only 0.407 GiB of routed expert bytes are read per token, while the dense part (Mamba NVFP4, Q8_0 attention, latent projections, output head, shared experts) is 4.09 GiB per token.

architecture.value: Nemotron-H hybrid Mamba-2 + Transformer LatentMoE plus C-RADIO v4-H vision encoder. config.json (BF16 repo): architectures NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3, llm_config NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM (model_type nemotron_h_puzzle), 88 blocks = 40 Mamba-2 + 40 MoE + 8 full-attention (block indices 7,16,25,36,47,58,69,78), hidden 4096, 32 query heads, num_key_value_heads 2, head_dim 128, no sliding window, Mamba 128 heads x 64 dim, state 128, 8 groups, conv 4; MoE: per-layer heterogeneous routed experts (240 to 496) with widths 1536-2560, 9 active, 1 shared expert (5376), moe_latent_size 1024, relu2, sigmoid routing, routed_scaling 5.0; vocab 131072. Quantization (GGUF and ModelOpt hf_quant_config): routed and shared experts IQ2_XXS (2.0625 bpw, QAT/QAD), Mamba in/out projections NVFP4 (W4A16), embeddings/output/attention/latent Q8_0. GGUF general.architecture = nemotron_h_moe.

context_length.value: 262144 (max_position_embeddings 262144; GGUF nemotron_h_moe.context_length 262144; card 'Up to 256K'). Long-context recovery trained at 128K. NVIDIA's 28GB recipe uses 65,536 with q8_0 KV; Unsloth's guide says 'Up to 128K for 74B-A9B'.

modalities.value: Input text, image, video; output text. Vision lives in a separate mmproj GGUF (1,733,692,736 B = 1.61 GiB) for llama.cpp, so omitting --mmproj (or passing --no-mmproj with -hf) gives a text-only path. In the safetensors repo the vision_model and mlp1 weights are inside the shards (no --language-model-only savings measured).

thinking.how_to_toggle: Chat template default enable_thinking=True (chat_template.jinja: 'set enable_thinking = enable_thinking if enable_thinking is defined else True'). Off: chat_template_kwargs {"enable_thinking": false} (template emits '<think></think>'). Medium effort: {"enable_thinking": true, "medium_effort": true} appends '{reasoning effort: efficient}' to the last user turn. llama.cpp b12407: per request body chat_template_kwargs (card's own llama.cpp client example), server default via --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' or --reasoning off; reasoning returned in reasoning_content. vLLM: same chat_template_kwargs per request, --default-chat-template-kwargs for a server default; card uses reasoning parser plugin ultra_v3 (ultra_v3_reasoning_parser.py in the repo, not in-tree; in-tree v0.33.0 has nemotron_v3). Ollama: tag lists thinking capability and parser nemotron-3-nano; native API 'think': true/false (per-request /v1 toggle not verified). History reasoning is re-inserted only from message.reasoning_content and is truncated for turns before the last user message (truncate_history_thinking default True).

tool_calling.evidence: chat_template.jinja (identical bytes in the GGUF tokenizer.chat_template, 12514 chars) contains the tool block and format instructions; card has a full llama.cpp tool-calling example with tool_choice auto/none; vLLM recipe uses --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder; llama.cpp b12407 common/chat.cpp lines 1420-1427 route templates containing '<tool_call>', '<function=', '<parameter=' to the Qwen3-Coder handler ('also used by Nemotron Nano 3, Qwen3.5'). Training card lists 26.2B tokens of tool-calling data and MCP E2E RL. Community 24GB-file run (anik-jha card, self-reported): BFCL simple valid/correct 100% / 94.3%, multiple 99.0% / 92.0%.

vllm.arch_supported: Yes at tag v0.33.0: registry.py line 553 'NemotronH_Omni_Reasoning_V3' -> nano_nemotron_vl; line 187 'NemotronHPuzzleForCausalLM' -> nemotron_h. The card's minimum is nightly 77154ca (2026-10-14), which v0.33.0 contains (GitHub compare: v0.33.0 is 843 commits ahead).
vllm.kv_math: Budget 16303 MiB x 0.92 = 14999 MiB = 14.65 GiB. Weights 22.43 GiB (HF API shard sum, includes vision; minus the ~1.61 GiB vision part it is still about 20.8 GiB). KV pool = 14.65 - 22.43 - 1.2 = -8.98 GiB, negative, so no context at all (also negative with --language-model-only). KV per token: 2 x 8 attention layers x 2 KV heads x 128 x 2 B = 8192 B BF16, 4096 B FP8; Mamba state per sequence about 40 x 128 x 64 x 128 x 2 B = 84 MB (bf16 ssm cache per card) plus conv state. If it fitted, 128k would cost 1.0 GiB BF16 KV. Expert CPU offload is not a usable plan (baseline: #66264).
vllm.quant_on_sm120: ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION with ggml-packed IQ2_XXS/Q8_0 blocks runs only through b12x kernels (docs/features/quantization/b12x.md at v0.33.0: 'uv pip install vllm[b12x]', --linear-backend b12x --moe-backend b12x; IQ2_XXS MoE with BF16 activations on SM120/SM121). Baseline: b12x is not installed in vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0. NVFP4 W4A16 Mamba layers would use Marlin.
vllm.reasoning_parser: ultra_v3 via --reasoning-parser-plugin ultra_v3_reasoning_parser.py (repo file); in-tree nemotron_v3 is the likely fallback (not verified for this model)
vllm.min_version: nightly-77154ca6116ae34cbfe314beef1016bde9b63989 per card (v0.33.0 is newer) plus pip b12x and 'vllm download-kernels'

vllm.known_issues: Needs b12x (absent from the image) and a 24 GB+ GPU; card lists A100/H100-80GB/Blackwell. FP8 KV on sm_120 goes through FlashInfer (baseline race #61239).

llamacpp.arch_supported: Yes. src/llama-arch.cpp at b12407 maps LLM_ARCH_NEMOTRON_H_MOE 'nemotron_h_moe' (line 105) and the latent tensors ffn_latent_down/ffn_latent_up (lines 584-585); src/models/nemotron-h.cpp loads per-layer expert counts and widths (lines 111-131). Support landed in PR #30520 'add Nemotron Super 3.5 VL and Nemotron Bolt 74B A9B support', merged 2026-10-15 (cd0a5b6a1); first build containing it is b11669. CUDA NVFP4 kernels present (ggml-cuda mmvq/mmq). The 'pixtral' pre-tokenizer bug in NVIDIA's GGUF (#30894) is fixed by PR #30960 (merged 2026-10-22), included in b12407. Spec types draft-dflash and draft-lilicorr exist at b12407 (common/speculative.cpp lines 77, 80).
llamacpp.quant: IQ2_XXS QAT (experts), NVFP4 Mamba, Q8_0 rest; no higher-quality smaller option exists because the QAT 2-bit file is the vendor's target
llamacpp.offload_plan: GGUF header arithmetic (range-read of the file header): non-routed tensors 4.617 GiB (incl. 0.531 GiB token_embd) stay on GPU; routed experts 15.882 GiB. VRAM budget about 15.3 GiB usable (16303 MiB minus ~0.11 GiB idle minus ~0.5 GiB CUDA context), target <= 14.8 GiB. KV f16 = 8192 B/token: 64k 0.50 GiB, 128k 1.00 GiB, 256k 2.00 GiB; q8_0 about 0.53x (256k q8_0 = 1.06 GiB). Mamba state ~0.16 GiB (-np 1). Compute buffers ~1.0 GiB. Fixed GPU at 128k f16 = 4.62 + 1.00 + 0.16 + 1.0 = 6.78 GiB, leaving ~8.0 GiB for experts. --n-cpu-moe 50 (blocks 0-49) puts 8.23 GiB of experts in RAM and 7.65 GiB on GPU: GPU total ~14.4 GiB. The same N gives 256k with -ctk/-ctv q8_0 (~14.5 GiB). For 64k f16, --n-cpu-moe 46 (7.61 GiB RAM, 8.27 GiB GPU, ~14.55 GiB). RAM use ~8.2 GiB experts plus ~1 GiB host buffers, far below the ~40 GiB free. Without --mmproj (text only). The LiLiCorr drafter would add 0.93 GiB on GPU and push ~2 more blocks to RAM; its benefit with CPU experts is unmeasured. Alternatively let --fit (default on) place experts by leaving -ncmoe unset.
llamacpp.server_command: docker run --rm --name bolt --device nvidia.com/gpu=all -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 --memory 24g -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -v $HOME/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 --hf-repo nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB-GGUF --hf-file NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Bolt-74B-A9B-24GB.gguf --no-mmproj --alias nemotron-bolt -c 131072 -np 1 -ngl 999 --n-cpu-moe 50 -fa on -b 2048 -ub 512 --jinja --temp 1.0 --top-p 0.95 --chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking":false}' --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080
llamacpp.tool_calling_note: Template is routed to llama.cpp's Qwen3-Coder XML handler (common/chat.cpp:1420-1427 at b12407); reasoning arrives in reasoning_content (OpenCode compatibility.reasoningField 'reasoning_content'). Same handler family as baseline issue #30118 (Qwen3.6 tool call leaking into content), so run a tool-call smoke test. Thinking is ON by default in the template, so set the server default off and enable per request via chat_template_kwargs.

ollama.context: 256K listed; Ollama default on <24 GiB GPUs is 4k, so OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 or more is required
ollama.capabilities: Manifest: model blob sha256:91d63363e782 = NVIDIA's GGUF byte-for-byte (22,018,326,528 B), projector 1,733,692,736 B, draft (architecture dflash) 998,242,560 B, so ~23.05 GiB total. Config: nemotron_h_moe, IQ2_XXS, 74.0B, renderer nemotron-3.5-super, parser nemotron-3-nano, requires 0.40.5 (baseline v0.40.16 is enough). Params: temperature 1, top_p 0.95, draft_num_predict 7. Search page shows vision, tools, thinking. On 16 GB Ollama falls back to whole-layer offload and also loads the projector and the draft, so expect it slower than llama.cpp --n-cpu-moe.

sampling: temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 (card 'Recommended Sampling', generation_config.json, GGUF general.sampling.temp/top_p, Ollama params). No min_p/top_k given. Unsloth guide uses defaults and gives no separate values for 74B-A9B. Thinking/no-thinking use the same values per the card.
speed_notes: Inferred decode bound at --n-cpu-moe 50: GPU reads 4.09 GiB dense + 0.19 GiB active experts = 4.27 GiB (4.59 GB) per token -> 5.1 ms at 896 GB/s; RAM reads 0.22 GiB (0.235 GB) of active experts -> 2.9 ms at 80 GB/s. Ceiling ~125 tok/s; at the ~69% efficiency implied by the community DGX Spark figure (40.1 tok/s vs 273/4.73 GB = 58 ceiling) expect roughly 55-80 tok/s single stream without speculation. Unlike most MoE models, the dense part (Mamba NVFP4 2.30 GiB, Q8_0 heads) dominates, so expert offload costs little; Qwen3.6-35B-A3B reads far fewer bytes per token and NVIDIA's own RTX Spark numbers show Bolt slower (84 vs 97 TPS, 601 s vs 454 s agent replay). Prefill with CPU experts is the open risk (baseline #25859).

opencode_fit.recommended_runtime: llama.cpp ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (Ollama fallback slower; vLLM does not fit)
opencode_fit.recommended_context: 131072 with f16 KV and --n-cpu-moe 50 (256k with q8_0 KV at the same N; 64k needs only N=46)
opencode_fit.caveats: Fits this laptop despite NVIDIA's 32 GB+ guidance because only ~8 GiB of experts need to live in RAM; the 32 GB figure assumes all-GPU plus drafter and mmproj. Everything is an estimate: nothing measured on sm_120 laptop. All quality numbers are NVIDIA-reported (TB2.1 50.98 vs Qwen3.6 44.38 in the same NVIDIA harness) with no independent AA/SWE-bench result; no SWE-bench Verified number is published. 2-bit QAT quality on long agentic sessions unknown. Thinking defaults ON and NVIDIA's agent replay is 32% slower than Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Tool calls go through llama.cpp's Qwen3-Coder XML handler (watch #30118-style leaks). Use OpenCode reasoningField 'reasoning_content'. Worth a measured head-to-head against pick #1.

gaps: Nothing run on this machine: VRAM, compute buffer size, tok/s and prefill at --n-cpu-moe 50 are estimates.
